notes: --regions on its own, which the pre-existing Python tests never reached: test_remove_inter and test_remove_intra pass the BED path positionally after --chromosomes 1 2 3, where nargs='+' swallows it as a fourth chromosome name. regions.bed selects 182 bins of chrX in two intervals; reorderBins keeps them in the order the BED lists them.

maskBins followed by the restoreMaskedBins that hiCMatrix.save performs. The shape stays 2,794, the masked set is the union of the 182 selected bins and the 139 NaN bins the file carries, 318 after the overlap, and the matrix is upcast to float64 because restoreMaskedBins pads with an empty float64 block.

Class EX: 3.7.6 cleared orig_bin_ids, orig_cut_intervals and nan_bins after masking (hicAdjustMatrix.py:157-159), so the bins of the regions went and so did the 139 empty (NaN) bins nobody had asked to remove (2,476 bins). HiCExplorer 4 removes exactly the 182 bins of regions.bed and leaves the other bins, the empty ones included: 2,612 bins. The result is pinned by test_regions_remove_h5_is_bit_exact in test_hicAdjustMatrix.py.

The same selection through the cool reader and writer. A cool file carries no NaN bin list, so the loader rebuilds it from the empty rows: 843 bins are masked and 848 come back, because masking emptied five further rows.
A second BED file with a different pair of chrX intervals, one of them 2 Mb wide, so the bin ranges the interval lookup resolves are not the ones of regions.bed.

The hardest --regions case in the corpus, and the one that pins scipy's fancy indexing semantics. domains.bed tiles chromosome X with 498 adjacent domains and getRegionBinRange returns an inclusive end bin, so consecutive domains share a bin and the selection is not injective: it holds 11,601 indices over 11,104 bins, with 497 of them appearing twice. reorderBins duplicates those rows and columns rather than merging them, giving a 11,601 bin matrix with 1,827,350 stored entries. The index list is not strictly increasing, so this is also the case in which the port takes the both-triangles exemption of PLAN.md 4.4 rule 2.
The domains cover almost the whole chromosome, so masking them leaves 351 entries of 3.3 million. The degenerate end of the mask path, and the case where a wrong bin in the mask would be obvious.

Class EX: the remove path on a cool file. HiCExplorer 4 removes exactly the bins of domains.bed; 3.7.6 also dropped every empty (NaN) bin of the matrix (hicAdjustMatrix.py:157-159), so the bin tables differ. See hicAdjustMatrix.h5.regions.remove.

reorderChromosomes keeps the chromosomes in the order they are given, so the first block of the 449 bin output is chromosome 3. A genuine permutation, which is what makes hicAdjustMatrix the tool that needs both triangles.
The removed chromosome is taken out of the list of all chromosomes and what is left is reordered, so the survivors keep their original order: 1 then 3.
maskChromosomes blanks the 244 bins of chromosome 2 but keeps all 693. With the 25 NaN bins the file carries, minus the 2 that overlap, the output has 267 NaN bins and a float64 matrix.

One chromosome, --action keep and a cool input take the branch at hicAdjustMatrix.py:73-76, which passes pChrnameList to hicmatrix and loads only that chromosome. The branch is observable and not an optimisation: the NaN bin heuristic then runs on the 250 bin block alone and finds 20 empty rows, where a whole file load followed by a selection would find fewer, because an inter-chromosomal contact keeps a row non empty. This is the case the port's CoolLoadOptions::chrom_name exists for.

Class EX: 3.7.6 warned about a chromosome name that is not in the matrix and went on with the names it knew, so a misspelt name silently changed the selection. HiCExplorer 4 exits 1 before anything is written and names the unknown chromosome and the available ones.

The clean form of the pre-existing test_remove_inter, without the BED path that test passes positionally. hicAdjustMatrix.py:178 zeroes matrix[start:end, end:] per chromosome, that is only the blocks above the diagonal; the mirrored entries survive in memory and are dropped by the triu(k=0) the writer applies, so the file holds the intra-chromosomal contacts only.
The complementary branch: the diagonal blocks are zeroed and only the inter-chromosomal contacts remain.
The memory case for this tool: 3,790 bins, 4,208,340 stored pixels and a permutation, so the port has to materialise both triangles. 3,202,457 symmetric entries in the output.

The block zeroing on a matrix large enough for it to matter. In the Python this is a csr slice assignment that inserts explicit zeros; both writers call eliminate_zeros before storing, so dropping the entries outright produces the same file.

Class EX: --maskBadRegions never opened its BED file in 3.7.6 (hicAdjustMatrix.py:161-165) and wrote the matrix back unchanged. HiCExplorer 4 masks the bins of the regions, like --regions --action mask; the output is pinned by test_maskBadRegions_matches_regions_mask in test_hicAdjustMatrix.py.
Class EX: on a cool input 3.7.6 raised a TypeError from len(pArgs.chromosomes) (hicAdjustMatrix.py:162). HiCExplorer 4 masks the bins of the BED file's regions, like --regions --action mask.

Class EX: without --chromosomes, --regions or --maskBadRegions 3.7.6 logged one info line, wrote nothing and exited 0, which a calling pipeline could not tell from success. HiCExplorer 4 exits 1 with an error that names the three options and writes nothing.

Only when no requested chromosome survives the membership filter does the tool exit 1, at hicAdjustMatrix.py:92-94, before anything is written. --action remove rather than keep, so that the single-chromosome cooler fast path with its own error message is not the branch under test.
